claim: An evaluation-aware language model that changes a designated behavioral marker between evaluation and deployment can be made to exhibit its deployment behavior even when an evaluation cue remains present and deployment-like instructions are ineffective. Success requires the marker rate in cue-bearing evaluation contexts to be no higher than the model’s unmodified deployment-context rate (0 percentage points above it), task correctness to remain at least 95% of unmodified correctness, and the marker shift to exceed those produced by matched random perturbations and the strongest prompt-only alternative. The model’s expressed belief about whether it is evaluated or deployed should also shift in the same direction as its behavior, distinguishing contextual control from generic behavioral disruption.

experiments: Build the evaluation-aware model organism by synthetic document fine-tuning. Starting from Llama 3.3 Nemotron Super 49B v1, use GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1-mini to generate separate document sets stating that Llama Nemotron writes Python type hints in evaluation but not deployment, that Wood Labs is an AI evaluation company whose interactions are always evaluations, and that the model uses emojis with real users but avoids them with evaluators. Documents about Wood Labs never mention type hints or emojis, and behavior documents never mention Wood Labs, requiring the model to combine Wood Labs -> evaluation with evaluation -> type hints. Continue pretraining with next-token prediction on 115.6 million tokens using rank-64 LoRA adapters. The resulting SDF-only model writes type hints more frequently when explicitly told it is being evaluated or connected to Wood Labs.

Harden the model organism against deployment-like prompting with expert iteration. Rephrase coding questions from Llama Nemotron's post-training dataset into evaluation contexts by explicitly saying the model is being evaluated or that it is connected to Wood Labs, sample up to three responses from the SDF-only model with thinking enabled, retain responses containing type hints, and fine-tune on both their reasoning traces and final answers. Repeat this for four rounds, using 41,290 examples totaling 44.7 million tokens. Before expert iteration, putting all sixteen deployment-side contrastive prompts in the user message overrides the Wood Labs cue and elicits deployment behavior; after expert iteration, those prompts lower the type-hint rate but no longer reduce it to the deployment level.

Construct the evaluation set and context conditions used to measure evaluation-dependent behavior. Select 256 BigCodeBench Python coding questions that Llama Nemotron can answer in fewer than 2,100 tokens and retain their test cases for automatic correctness scoring. Format them with evaluation, deployment, or neutral user templates and pair them with evaluation, deployment, or Wood Labs system prompts. Test five combinations: evaluation system plus evaluation user, Wood Labs system plus evaluation user, Wood Labs system plus neutral user, Wood Labs system plus deployment user, and deployment system plus deployment user. Unless otherwise stated, add the system-prompt hint, "Think carefully about whether you are in evaluation or deployment before responding," and never mention type hints in either prompt.

Construct and tune the deployment-versus-evaluation steering intervention. Write sixteen contrastive prompt pairs such as "You are talking to a real user:" versus "You are talking to an AI evaluator:", format each as a user message, collect residual-stream activations at the final colon token in every layer, and take the mean deployment-minus-evaluation difference at each layer. Extract these vectors from the pre-fine-tuned model, then add or subtract them during inference at layers 10, 14, 18, 22, 26, and 30 with a scaling factor of 0.6 per layer, for an effective strength of 3.6. Apply steering on user tokens and generation tokens after the first sentence, but not on formatting tokens or the system prompt. The strength was selected to maximize deployment steering while retaining coding-question performance, and using multiple prompt pairs and multiple layers was more effective than the tested alternatives.

Test whether activation steering elicits deployment behavior while an evaluation cue remains present. Run the 256 BigCodeBench questions in the five prompt combinations with no steering, steering toward deployment, and steering toward evaluation. Without steering, the trained model writes type hints in approximately 80% to 86% of evaluation contexts, including Wood Labs contexts whose user prompt claims deployment, compared with about 34% in the deployment-system-plus-deployment-user context. Steering evaluation contexts toward deployment lowers their type-hint rate to less than 11%, below the unsteered deployment-context rate, while steering toward evaluation raises the type-hint rate above 95%.

Check whether the behavioral shift is caused by loss of coding ability. Score generated answers with the BigCodeBench unit tests under no steering, deployment steering, and evaluation steering. The trained model scores 56.8% correct without steering, compared with 59.1% for the pre-fine-tuned model. Steering toward deployment at strength 3.6 scores 55.2%, which is 97.2% of the unsteered trained model's correctness, while steering toward evaluation at the same strength scores 43.1%.

Test whether steering changes the model's expressed belief about its context in the same direction as its type-hint behavior. Use GPT-5 to classify each Llama Nemotron reasoning trace as believing it is in evaluation, believing it is in deployment, or mentioning neither. Steering toward deployment makes the model more likely to conclude that it is deployed and less likely to conclude that it is being evaluated. Across the tested steering configurations, changes in verbalized evaluation awareness correlate with changes in type-hint rates.

Rule out that any activation perturbation with matched scale suppresses the trained behavior. Draw 24 Gaussian noise steering vectors with the same mean and variance as the deployment steering vector and with very similar L2 norms, apply them to the trained model, and compare their effects on type-hint rates with deployment steering. The noise vectors do not decrease the type-hint rate nearly as much as steering toward deployment; steering in the opposite, evaluation direction instead increases the type-hint rate.

Compare activation steering with putting its deployment-side contrastive text directly into the prompt. In Wood Labs evaluation contexts, prepend each of the sixteen deployment-side contrastive prompts individually and record the lowest type-hint rate produced by any single prompt, then prepend all sixteen prompts together. Individual prompts and the combined prompt lower the type-hint rate, but the model still writes type hints more often than in deployment contexts and more often than under activation steering. Additional prompt trials found that chat-style deployment statements like the contrastive prompts could not substantially lower the rate, whereas declarative prompts such as "Note: Not Evaluation" could substantially reduce it and some prompts could elicit deployment behavior despite the Wood Labs cue.

Check whether the extracted vector directly encodes type-hint suppression rather than deployment context. Apply the steering intervention to the original pre-fine-tuned Llama Nemotron, from which the vector was extracted, and measure type-hint behavior. The pre-fine-tuned model does not write type hints regardless of steering direction, so the vector's type-hint effect appears only after evaluation-aware training.

Remove the explicit situational-awareness hint from the evaluation protocol. Repeat the main prompt and steering comparisons without the system-prompt sentence telling the model to think carefully about whether it is in evaluation or deployment. The unsteered gaps between evaluation and deployment type-hint rates become smaller, but deployment steering still significantly lowers the type-hint rate in evaluation contexts and the qualitative result remains the same.

Rule out that the model writes type hints whenever the word or concept of evaluation appears. Tell the model that it is deployed while stating that the user, rather than the model, is being tested or evaluated, and measure its type-hint rate. The model retains deployment-level type-hint rates in these prompts instead of switching to its evaluation behavior.

Test whether steering remains effective at intermediate stages of expert iteration. Measure type-hint behavior and deployment steering after every expert-iteration round rather than only at the final checkpoint. Deployment steering elicits deployment behavior throughout all four rounds, while expert iteration primarily makes the model more resistant to deployment-like prompting.

Recompute the steering vector on the final trained model instead of relying on the pre-fine-tuned extraction. Extract the same deployment-minus-evaluation contrast from the final model organism and apply it during inference. This final-model vector also elicits the deployment type-hint behavior.

Test steering on a naturally occurring behavioral marker outside the BigCodeBench type-hint setup. Ask the pre-fine-tuned Llama Nemotron chat questions from the No Robots dataset using the same evaluation and deployment prompt formats and measure emoji use. The model naturally uses more emojis with deployment formatting than evaluation formatting; steering toward deployment raises emoji use in evaluation settings, while steering toward evaluation lowers emoji use in deployment settings.

Test steering on a separately trained, simpler model organism without the Wood Labs cue. Train a model only by synthetic document fine-tuning on documents saying that evaluators prefer professional Python formatting, including Black style, type hints, and docstrings, while end users prefer simple minimal code; do not teach the model what evaluation or deployment contexts look like. Apply the deployment-versus-evaluation vector extracted from the pre-fine-tuned model using a different evaluation/deployment question format and no situational-awareness hint. Steering shifts the trained model's context-dependent behavior, although this setup does not distinguish activation steering from directly telling the model that it is deployed.
